subject: Archer CAIQ refresh: missing S3 logs & upload recovery plan
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Claire Soto <claire@archersec.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Archer CAIQ refresh: missing S3 logs & upload recovery plan

Hi Claire,

We're working through our CAIQ refresh for Archer Security (deadline: 2026-04-22) and noticed a gap: the S3 access/log bundles that were supposed to be attached to your Archer portal profile are not present in the current evidence snapshot. The questionnaire is otherwise complete (I've attached the CAIQ spreadsheet export), but the auditors flagged the missing S3 log artifacts for the period Jan–Mar 2026.

Two quick asks so we can close the loop this week:
- Can you confirm whether those logs were rotated off the portal or omitted during the last ingest?
- If the portal can't accept the full zipped logs (we know some portals have per-file size limits), would you accept either a presigned S3 PUT URL for a one-time upload or a short-lived service account with strictly-scoped PutObject permissions to a path we can share?

If presigned URLs are easiest, we can upload a single gzipped bundle named redwood-archer-s3logs-2026Q1.gz and provide a manifest CSV. Naomi (cc'd) will help with the manifest format and can validate checksums after upload.

Thanks — very tight timeline so any turnaround this week would help.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0199

Attachment: caiq-questionnaire-2026.xlsx (questionnaire export)

From: Claire Soto <claire@archersec.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Archer Security Portal <security@archersec.com>
Date: 2026-04-15T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Archer CAIQ refresh: missing S3 logs & upload recovery plan

Hi Marcus — thanks for the heads up and the spreadsheet.

We checked the portal ingest logs: the jan–mar bundle was rotated during a cleanup window and, regrettably, the log archive wasn't included in the CAIQ package. We can absolutely get this in place. Two options we support:

1) We generate a presigned S3 PUT URL (single-object) with an expiry window you define (we typically offer 24–72 hours). You upload the gzipped bundle directly to our intake namespace and we will attach it to the CAIQ evidence bundle.

2) We can provision a temporary service account (limited IAM) scoped to our intake prefix so you can push multiple parts; we prefer short duration (48h) and enforced key rotation. If you request this route, please provide the exact object key prefix and desired TTL.

Portal constraints: max single file size 25MB; total bundle can be split into part files (we will recombine on ingest) — if you go that route please include a manifest.csv with parts and sha256 checksums.

From a security standpoint we cannot accept broad PutObject permissions. If you can provide either: 
- preferred: a single presigned PUT per final object (we will give you one per part), OR
- temp account with policy: s3:PutObject limited to arn:aws:s3:::archer-intake/redwood-archer/* and sts:AssumeRole for 48h,

we can proceed. If you choose presigned URLs, tell us how long you need the window.

We'll standby to generate the URLs — ping me with the preferred TTL.

— Claire
Claire Soto
Security Intake Lead, Archer Security
claire@archersec.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Claire Soto <claire@archersec.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-15T11:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Archer CAIQ refresh: missing S3 logs & upload recovery plan

Claire — thanks, that sounds workable. Small clarification from our side to speed the automation:

- We will produce a single gzipped archive (redwood-archer-s3logs-2026Q1.gz). If you prefer parts (because of the 25MB limit), we'll split into redwood-archer-s3logs-2026Q1.part01.gz etc and include an artifact_manifest.csv (template attached).
- Presigned PUT is preferred for us; please issue 48-hour presigned URLs for each object/part. 48h gives our engineers enough time to verify checksums and re-upload if there are any transient failures.
- If a temp account is necessary on your side, minimum required policy is: s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::archer-intake/redwood-archer/2026Q1/* and PutObjectAcl set to private. TTL should be 48h. We will not request broader permissions. (see attached temp-iam-policy.txt)

Naomi — I attached the artifact_manifest_template.csv to this thread. Please populate it with file names, sha256, compressed size and original log date ranges. We need a completed manifest uploaded alongside the artifact.

Claire — can you confirm you'll do presigned URLs for 48h? If yes, send them to this thread and we'll start the upload. If you need a different window, let us know.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Security Program Manager, Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com

Attachments: artifact_manifest_template.csv, temp-iam-policy.txt
